claim: Keeping an archive of promising states and returning to them before exploring solves hard-exploration problems that curiosity-driven agents fail. Atari Montezuma: Phase 1 mean 57,439 (57% of 100 runs solved level 1, no domain knowledge); intrinsic-motivation prior best about 17,500. Salimans and Chen reached 74,500 from one demonstration with the same restart idea.
agent_test: Compare, at equal tokens, a flat retry loop against a loop that stores partial solutions and restarts from the best one on a task with a checker.
audit_note: Go-Explore Phase 1 relies on restoring simulator states (stated by the authors), not noted in the claim; numbers 57,439, 57%, 17,500 and 74,500 match.

claim: The cell (state key) design is the main lever. Adding easy domain knowledge cut the cost of solving Montezuma level 1 from 640M to 57.6M frames (about 11x) and raised the Phase 1 mean from 57,439 to 148,220. A generic downscaled-image cell found only 22 Pitfall rooms.
agent_test: Vary the key used to dedupe archive entries (raw text, normalised answer, plan skeleton) and measure distinct useful entries per 100k tokens.
audit_note: Pitfall 22-room figure is the no-domain-knowledge Phase 1 result; 640M to 57.6M and 57,439 to 148,220 match.

claim: A key that is too coarse merges different states and starves the archive. In LLM red-teaming 96% of attack intents mapped to one cell under a tool-name-only hash; in Pitfall, visually identical screens needing different actions broke the image cell.
agent_test: Log archive collisions: how many distinct candidate plans share a key. Add one disambiguating feature and test again.

claim: Exploring after reaching an archived state (post-exploration) helps. MiniGrid FourRooms, LavaCrossing, LavaGap: on beat off on all three, and mattered more than tuning epsilon. Ablating post-goal exploration in the Latent Go-Explore maze lowered coverage significantly.
agent_test: After restoring a stored partial solution, allow a fixed short free-exploration burst (about 20 steps in Yang et al.) versus none, at equal tokens.

claim: Derailment has direct support in only one study: in 18 of 20 count-based intrinsic-reward robot runs, visit counts dropped 10x between grasp and lift, so rarely visited cells were not revisited. No replication outside the Go-Explore group.
agent_test: Not directly testable on a language agent. Test the consequence instead: does a resample-from-scratch arm lose frontier states that an archive arm keeps.

claim: Raw archive trajectories are not valid results; they must be robustified. Single-demonstration robustification worked in 40% of attempts; in 51 of 57 level-1 runs the best path used a game bug. Failure-finding work on driving also needed a robustify step.
agent_test: Re-run every archived solution on a mutated or held-out input before it counts; track how many fail (G3 check).

claim: A language model that picks which archived state to resume, which action to try, and what to archive (Intelligent Go-Explore, IGE) beats ReAct and Reflexion on long-horizon text tasks. Cooking Game 92 vs ReAct 56, Reflexion 52; Coin Collector about 88 vs 0 for all others; BabyAI put-next-to 84 vs 48; Game of 24 100 vs 82 (ReAct) and 83 (Reflexion). GLoW, a different team using a value-ranked frontier, beat IGE on some Jericho games (Enchanter 61.7 vs 50.0). Caveat from re-implementation: at 1,000 steps and about equal API cost on Jericho (GPT-4.1-mini), IGE beat ReAct on some games (Deephome 71.3 vs 11.0, Detective 316.7 vs 113.3) and not on others (Zork1 44.3 vs 48.3, Ztuu 15.0 vs 18.7). All IGE comparisons are at equal steps or operations, not equal tokens.
agent_test: Build a small frontier of partial solutions with an LLM picking the resume point; compare with ReAct and best-of-N at equal total tokens on Game of 24 and one ARC subset.

claim: Which LLM-driven step matters depends on horizon. Game of 24 (short): without LLM action choice 68, without all three 61. BabyAI Put Next To: without action choice 24, without state choice 48, without filtering 64, without all three 4, without action history 72. Classic visitation-count Go-Explore: 38 on Game of 24, 4 on BabyAI, 0 on Cooking.
agent_test: Ablate resume-point choice and archive filtering separately on a short and a long task; check the horizon dependence.

claim: Archive bloat is real and filtering controls it. Native Go-Explore holds 2,839 cells at Montezuma score 2500 vs 566 for time-myopic; Gravitar 7,376 vs 381. IGE filtering cut archive size from 203.5 to 25.5 states (BabyAI) and 22.4 to 4.4 (Cooking), but only 18.5 to 15.6 on Game of 24.
agent_test: Cap archive size, filter by code or one cheap model call, and measure tokens per step as the archive grows.

claim: The archive loop helps most for weaker base models. Game of 24 naive to IGE: Claude Sonnet 3.5 24 to 86, Llama-3 400B 44 to 98, GPT-4 70 to 100. Against Reflexion on Sonnet 3.5 (80 vs 86) the gain is not significant. Update: no re-measure with current frontier models was found. Neighbouring evidence is mixed: Go-Browse resume benefit is larger for the weaker solver (figure), SWE-Search relative gain is smallest for GPT-4o (+17% vs +22 to +27%), SOAR refinement gain over sampling does not shrink from 7B to 123B (+6.5 to +12.4 points), and the one test on a current cheap model (Haiku 4.5) found the archive losing to retry (K23).
agent_test: Check the gain at two model strengths; expect it to shrink as the plain model improves.

claim: Domain-general prompts cost little: IGE on Game of 24 scored 96% with no hints vs 100% tuned. Malformed model outputs were under 0.1% of actions.
agent_test: Use the generic prompt first; add hints only if they win at equal tokens.

claim: An archive of whole agents with open-ended parent choice beats greedy or latest-only. Darwin Godel Machine, 80 iterations: SWE-bench 50.0 vs greedy 39.7 vs no-archive 23.0 vs no self-improvement 39.0; Polyglot 38.0 vs 30.0 vs 14.0 vs 28.0. Share of kept working agents 51.3% vs 32.5%. One run per arm; about 22,000 USD for one SWE-bench run.
agent_test: Not at our scale. Borrow only the parent rule (weight by score and by few children) for choosing which stored partial solution to resume.

claim: The archive lets search pass through temporary score drops: DGM children scoring below their parent at iterations 4 and 56 later led to new bests. Anecdote from one run. Update: HGM finds that a parent's own score correlates only 0.28 to 0.44 with how well its descendants do (SWE-Verified-60, Polyglot), which supports the mechanism but not a count of how often low-scoring resumes pay off. Still no controlled count.
agent_test: Allow resuming from a lower-scoring stored entry once; log whether it ever leads to the final answer.

claim: Heuristic add-ons to archive search can interfere. In LLM red-teaming a reward bonus with granular signatures cut findings by 94% (161 findings), reward alone gave 18 false positives and 0 attacks, and all three enhancements together gave zero findings.
agent_test: Add archive heuristics one at a time and keep each only if it wins at equal tokens.

claim: Seed variance can exceed algorithm effects in an LLM archive search: 0 to 16 findings across 5 seeds (8x); seed 42 gave 16 vs a 5-seed mean of 4.6; the mean stabilised after 3 to 4 seeds. Single-seed comparisons are unreliable. IGE used 25 seeds per task and 100 on Game of 24.
agent_test: Evaluate every archive variant on at least 25 problems with repeated runs; never conclude from one run.

claim: Many short independent runs add diversity until about N=20 (4 attack types); after that only duplicates grow (1054 attacks at N=100). Scope note: this counts distinct attack types. On checkable tasks, solved-problem coverage keeps rising log-linearly with samples over several orders of magnitude (K32), so do not read N=20 as a general saturation point.
agent_test: Spend the first 20 or so attempts on diversity, then switch to depth on the best entry.

claim: Learned or cell-free state keys approximate but do not clearly match hand-built cells. Authors report parity or gains, yet in the numbers native Go-Explore beats time-myopic on Montezuma at 1M frames (2303 vs 695) and Frostbite (11,721 vs 3,543), and LGE found about 5k Montezuma cells, below full Go-Explore.
agent_test: Compare a learned key (embedding distance of candidate plans) with a hand key on archive size and coverage.

claim: Go-Explore without simulator restore still beats prior state of the art (Montezuma 97,728, Pitfall 20,093 after policy-based return), but scores far below the restore version (Pitfall 102,571). Restore is an assumption, not the whole gain.
agent_test: For an LLM agent restore is free (stored text), so the restore gap does not apply; test only the selection rule.

claim: Go-Explore finds failures in long-horizon driving tests where MCTS and deep RL find none, but MCTS beats it at medium horizon.
agent_test: Use archives for long-horizon tasks only; for short tasks a tree or plain resampling may win (G12).

claim: Plain LLM agents explore poorly: Reflexion did not beat ReAct on long text games and sometimes hurt, and open-weight reasoning models loop in text mazes (Qwen3-235B coverage 52.7% easy, 23.0% medium).
agent_test: Include a plain retry-with-reflection arm; expect an archive arm to beat it on long tasks only.

claim: Update 2026-10-26: still no measured IGE-style archive of partial reasoning steps (proof steps, math chains) with an LLM picking the resume state. Near neighbours now exist: a Go-Explore-style sandbox-snapshot archive for coding agents (lost to retry, K23), and checker-guided refine or population search on ARC, planning and code (K24, K25). Original wording: no measured Go-Explore variant for pure reasoning or code steps beyond Game of 24 in IGE. This is an absence in the search tools used, not a proof.
agent_test: Run our own archive-of-partial-solutions arm on ARC and a reasoning set as the first measurement.

claim: Prompt-space MAP-Elites archives (Rainbow Teaming) reach high attack success (about 92% on Llama 2 and 3, 98% on Mistral 7B and Vicuna 7B after 2000 iterations) with about 50% transfer, using a text-similarity filter (threshold 0.6 dropped about 24% of candidates). No ablation against a no-archive arm was read.
agent_test: Dedupe stored candidates by text similarity before adding; measure whether it raises distinct-idea count at equal tokens.

claim: At equal total tokens an archive of resumable states can lose to plain independent retry. Coding agents (Claude Haiku 4.5, Terminal-Bench 2.0, 5 tasks x 5 seeds, 1M tokens each): retry 17/25 (68%) vs snapshot-branching 6/25 (24%). Causes named by the authors: budget split between root and children, wrong-state attractors, handoff cost, weak progress signals. Resuming did rescue 67% of failed roots on one task.
agent_test: Run the archive arm against retry and best-of-N at equal total tokens, root and selection calls included. Adopt it only where it wins; start with stuck-state cases.

claim: On ARC-style program synthesis with a checker, breadth is the strong baseline at small budgets and refinement or archive gains appear at larger budgets. At 128 calls repeated sampling led (GPT-4o 15.0 vs tree variants 8.7 to 14.0; DeepSeek-V3 18.6 vs 10.0 to 18.3). At 6,000 candidates, half refinements beat all fresh samples (7B 14.25 vs 5.63; 72B 25.62 vs 18.50). Budgets counted in calls or candidates, not tokens.
agent_test: Spend a first slice of the budget on independent samples, then switch to resuming and refining the best entries; log the switch point.

claim: Checker-guided population search over whole candidate solutions beat best-of-N and sequential revision on natural-language planning with cost reported: TravelPlanner 95.6% vs 55.6% (best-of-N) at $0.29 vs $0.47 per instance; Trip Planning 96.2% vs 77.2% at $0.17 vs $0.10; Meeting Planning 85.0% vs 69.4% at $0.52 vs $0.39 (Gemini 1.5 Flash). Needs an exact evaluator; not an archive of resumable partial states.
agent_test: Use a code-run checker as the fitness signal for any archive loop; if no checker exists, expect the gain to vanish (see K33).

claim: Choosing the resume point by best score alone loses to rules that also credit few children or descendant results. DGM greedy 39.7 vs 50.0 (SWE-bench) and 30.0 vs 38.0 (Polyglot); ShinkaEvolve weighted sampling beats hill climbing, which plateaus; HGM clade score correlates 0.78 and 0.63 with true descendant productivity vs 0.29 to 0.44 for score-based rules. Selection in all three is by code, not by the model.
agent_test: Resume rule: weight = sigmoid(score) / (1 + number of children), later replaced by descendant results once there are enough; selector in code, never the generating model (G8).
audit_note: Score-based rule correlations span 0.27 to 0.44 (Polyglot SICA is 0.274), not 0.29 to 0.44; minor rounding slip.

claim: A cheap code-embedding similarity filter (reject above 0.95) gave most of the gain of a model novelty judge in a program archive; the extra LLM judge was 'marginal' (ShinkaEvolve, circle packing, effect read from a figure). Archive sizes were 10 to 50 programs. Native Go-Explore filtering by cell and IGE filtering by model remain the other two designs seen.
agent_test: Start with code dedupe (normalised text or output equality) plus a size cap; add a model novelty judge only if an equal-token test shows it pays.

claim: Showing the generator every earlier entry does not help and can hurt. ADAS-style agent search: all prior agents 55.0 average best score vs ignoring prior designs 60.0 vs top-7 by score 60.3 (MGSM best agent 41.4 vs 56.2 vs 56.5). Top-k raised score but lowered diversity; ignoring the archive gave the most diverse set.
agent_test: Show the resumed run only its own entry plus at most a few top entries; keep one arm that sees none.

claim: After resuming, a few short bursts beat both one burst and long commitment, for an LLM agent in text games: 50-step bursts, 1,000 steps total, best at 3 bursts per selected state (Zork1 73.0 vs 59.0 at 1 burst and 59.3 at 5; Ludicorp 73.7 vs 34.0 and 53.3). Part of the effect is the reflection step that needs more than one burst. No comparison with restarting from the root at equal tokens.
agent_test: Default resume = about 3 short attempts from the stored state before the next selection; re-tune on our tasks.

claim: Restoring a state also restores its mistakes. Faithful restore makes a plausible but wrong partial solution sticky; a fresh agent re-pays understanding (child 190k tokens over 26 steps vs 90k over 11 for a successful fresh retry); progress proxies such as installed packages or claimed completion mislead the selector.
agent_test: Archive only entries that passed a check, store why the entry is believed good, and let the resumed run challenge it once before building on it.

claim: No head-to-head test of state keys for a reasoning agent exists. Keys that worked in neighbouring work: URL for web pages (Go-Browse), grouping programs by their output grid (SOAR), git diff or replayed commands when progress is in files, full snapshot only when progress is in a database (Graviet: 4/5 vs 0/5 on the planted task).
agent_test: Test three keys on one checkable set: normalised answer, plan skeleton, execution output on the checker inputs; measure cell count and share in the largest cell.

claim: Solved-problem coverage keeps rising with independent samples far past 20: roughly log-linear over several orders of magnitude (CodeContests Gemma-2B 0.02% to 7.1% at 10,000 samples; SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250). Plateaus appear later and depend on method and model: repeated sampling on ARC begins to plateau around 200 to 500 calls (budget tested up to 512), the 7B search in SOAR flattens near 5.2k attempts.
agent_test: Do not cap parallel independent runs at 20 when a checker exists; choose N by the measured coverage curve on a pilot slice.
audit_note: AB-MCTS paper says repeated sampling on ARC only begins to plateau while AB-MCTS keeps improving between 200 and 500 calls (figure, budget capped at 512); it does not show flat beyond about 500.
claim_before_audit: Solved-problem coverage keeps rising with independent samples far past 20: log-linear over four orders of magnitude (CodeContests Gemma-2B 0.02% to 7.1% at 10,000 samples; SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250). Plateaus appear later and depend on method and model: repeated sampling on ARC flattens beyond about 500 calls, the 7B search in SOAR flattens near 5.2k attempts.

claim: The picker of the final answer must be a real check, not a vote or a model score. MATH, Llama-3-8B: coverage 82.9% to 98.44% from 100 to 10,000 samples, but majority vote or reward model only 40.50% to 41.41%. SWE-Search: model value estimate chose the right solution 73% of the time, a separate discriminator 84%. Supports G8 for archive and final choice.
agent_test: Final pick = code-run checker where one exists; otherwise a different model or prompt than the generator, never the generator's own score.

claim: Archived programs can pass the shown examples and still be wrong: SOAR found solutions that hard-code outputs and are brittle, and filters them by checking whether computed outputs appear in the code. No study reports the share of archived solutions that fail on mutated or held-out input.
agent_test: Re-run each archived solution on a mutated input before it can be resumed or returned; log the failure share.

claim: Returning to a stored state beats re-deriving it, most for deeper states and weaker solvers: Go-Browse prefixed sampling (start at the stored page) gave higher success than starting from the home page, with the largest difference for Qwen-2.5-7B and for deeper pages (figure, no table); resetting to 15 stored pages instead of 1 raised unique URLs from 183 to 260 at equal task count; a feasibility check saved 13% of steps.
agent_test: Store the shortest verified path to each entry so a resume costs a replay, not a re-derivation.

claim: Return inside a single reasoning trace has a small measured benefit in RL training: restarting rollouts from high-entropy prefixes (FR3E) gave +1.8 to +3.1 average points over GRPO++ on eight math benchmarks, nothing on AIME24 for a math-specialised base. Training result, cost not matched.
agent_test: Candidate resume points inside a chain: steps where the model's own samples disagree. Test as a scaffold before relying on it.
